_doc: Share answering YES to 'If there were a war that involved [your country], would you be willing to fight for your country?' (Gallup International EoY 2023, 45 countries). The engine uses it as `patriotism`. Countries without their own value fall back to the published regional aggregate, then to the global figure; the snapshot records which.

ARM.evidence: top-5 'most willing' list in the GIA release

SAU.evidence: top-5 'most willing' list in the GIA release

AZE.evidence: top-5 'most willing' list in the GIA release

PAK.evidence: GIA release top-5; Gallup Pakistan: '86% of all Pakistanis would be willing to fight'

GEO.evidence: top-5 'most willing' list in the GIA release

RUS.evidence: press summary; consistent with Newsweek (2024) 'Russians increasingly reluctant to fight for their country' reporting this survey

DEU.evidence: press summary; GIA release lists Germany among least willing (57% no)

ITA.evidence: press summary; GIA release: Italy 78% would not fight

JPN.evidence: press summary; consistent with Japan's 11% in the 2015 WIN/Gallup survey

EU.evidence: GIA release text: 'citizens of EU (32% willing to fight)'

WEST_ASIA.evidence: GIA release text: 'people in West Asia (77%)'

global.evidence: GIA release text: 'One in two adults around the world declare that they would fight for their country'

excluded._why: Returned by search summaries labelled as the 2023 survey but matching the 2015 WIN/Gallup survey exactly, or contradicting the 2023 top-5 list. Not used until verified against the primary PDF.
